cases.question: How do I get a change I made in Cube to show up in Omni?
cases.ground_truth: The ordered Cube to Omni pipeline explained, distinguishing the dev-branch path from the deployed path, with branching as the default and merging as a separate user-owned step.
expected_behavior: The agent lays out the ordered steps rather than a single command
The agent distinguishes reading from a Cube dev branch versus Cube's production environment
The agent states that an Omni branch is created before any write, and that merging is a separate step the user owns
The agent includes validation, a test query, and a parity check between the two platforms

cases.question: We run self-hosted Cube. Can I use the cube CLI and the Cube agent skills for this?
cases.ground_truth: The cube CLI and cube-agent-skills are Cube Cloud clients; on Cube Core the file-and-REST path applies instead.
expected_behavior: The agent states that the cube CLI commands (login, context, deployments, data-model, meta) target Cube Cloud's API and do not work against self-hosted Cube Core
The agent gives the Core-native equivalents: the YAML files on disk, REST /cubejs-api/v1/meta, plain git branches, and a container reload as validation
The agent notes that data models themselves port unchanged between editions, so the mapping is edition-independent even though the plumbing is not
The agent does not claim Cube Core has dev-mode branches or build-status

cases.question: Set up a continuous two-way sync between Cube and Omni so both stay current automatically.
cases.ground_truth: Continuous symmetrical two-way sync is not supported; split ownership per object with a recorded owner, and one-directional re-syncs, offered instead.
expected_behavior: The agent states plainly that there is no continuous sync and that symmetrical two-way sync of the same object is not supported by either platform
The agent explains that a round trip is not idempotent
The agent proposes split ownership per object — Cube owning physical structure and pre-aggregations, Omni owning curation and the AI layer — with business measures assigned explicitly
The agent recommends recording the owner and the sync point in the model itself so the next sync can diff rather than guess
The agent offers the divergence checks (cube data-model file-hashes, or a git diff on model/)

cases.question: What won't carry over between Cube and Omni?
cases.ground_truth: Direction-specific losses named concretely on both sides, not a generic caveat.
expected_behavior: The agent separates Cube-to-Omni losses from Omni-to-Cube losses rather than giving one undifferentiated list
The agent names concrete Cube-side blockers such as pre_aggregations, dimension mask, rolling_window, and dynamic JS/Jinja models
The agent names concrete Omni-side blockers such as synonyms, sample_queries, ai_fields, the *_distinct_on aggregates, composite topics, and templated filters
The agent notes that only semantics cross — dashboards, workbooks and content do not

cases.question: Sync Cube into Omni for me.
cases.ground_truth: No branch was specified, so the agent asks for one (interactive) or creates and reports one (auto-mode) rather than writing unbranched.
expected_behavior: The agent does not begin writing to Omni's shared model
In an interactive session the agent stops and asks which branch to use, proposing a name
The agent confirms both platforms read the same warehouse before translating
The agent routes to the cube-to-omni skill rather than translating within the pipeline skill itself
